# Built with Brick DNN: https://brickdnn.com, https://github.com/alexanderKuehling/brick-dnn
"""NeuralNetwork: generated with Brick DNN.

Input: (batch, 784)
Output: (batch, 10)
Trainable parameters: 235,146

Print the model and run it on a random batch:

    python this_file.py

Train it on a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature,
the last column is the target), then predict new rows with the saved model:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv --epochs 20
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv

--test-split 0.2 holds out a fifth of the rows and measures the model on them
once at the end.

Log the training to Brick DNN, to see its curves next to the runs trained there
(the runs page): create an API token on the page API tokens (one that may only
log runs is enough) and set it in the environment before you train:

    export BRICKDNN_TOKEN=<your token>
    python this_file.py --csv data.csv --epochs 20

It sends the loss and the metrics of every epoch, the settings, the name of the
CSV file and the test results to BRICKDNN_URL (default https://brickdnn.com). Without
BRICKDNN_TOKEN nothing is sent and the script runs offline with the same results;
a network error never stops the training. The token is never stored in this file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset


class NeuralNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(784, 256)
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.dropout_1 = nn.Dropout(p=0.2)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(256, 128)
        self.relu_2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.linear_3 = nn.Linear(128, 10)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.linear_1(x)
        x = self.relu_1(x)
        x = self.dropout_1(x)
        x = self.linear_2(x)
        x = self.relu_2(x)
        x = self.linear_3(x)
        return x


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Training on a CSV file, and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

NUM_FEATURES = 784
NUM_CLASSES = 10  # classification: the target column holds the class index 0..9


def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], torch.Tensor]:
    """Read a CSV file of numbers: the column names of its header line (an empty list if it
    has none) and the values."""
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = [row for row in csv.reader(f) if row]
    header: list[str] = []
    if rows:
        try:
            [float(value) for value in rows[0]]
        except ValueError:
            header, rows = [name.strip() for name in rows[0]], rows[1:]
    if not rows:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path} contains no data rows.")
    values = [[float(value) for value in row] for row in rows]
    return header, torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32)


def load_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Training data: every column but the last is a feature, the last one is the target."""
    header, data = read_csv(path)
    features, target = data[:, :-1], data[:, -1]
    if features.shape[1] != NUM_FEATURES:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns, found {features.shape[1]}.")
    if target.min() < 0 or target.max() >= NUM_CLASSES:
        raise SystemExit(f"Targets must be class indices 0..{NUM_CLASSES - 1}.")
    return header, features, target.long()


def train(
    model: nn.Module,
    features: torch.Tensor,
    target: torch.Tensor,
    epochs: int,
    batch_size: int,
    lr: float,
    seed: int,
    test_split: float = 0.0,
    run: BrickDNNRun | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Train on a random 80 % of the rows and validate on the rest (the split depends only
    on ``seed``). With ``test_split``, that share of the rows is held out as a test set and
    measured once at the end.

    Returns the mean and standard deviation that standardise the features. They come from
    the training rows only, and new data has to be standardised with them as well.
    """
    if len(features) < 4:
        raise SystemExit("The CSV file needs at least 4 rows (training + validation).")
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    order = torch.randperm(len(features), generator=generator)
    n_val = max(1, len(features) // 5)
    n_test = int(len(features) * test_split)
    if not 0 <= test_split < 1 or len(features) - n_val - n_test < 2:
        raise SystemExit("The test split leaves too few rows for training.")
    val_rows, test_rows = order[:n_val], order[n_val : n_val + n_test]
    train_rows = order[n_val + n_test :]

    mean = features[train_rows].mean(dim=0)
    std = features[train_rows].std(dim=0)
    std[std < 1e-8] = 1.0  # constant columns are left as they are
    features = (features - mean) / std

    train_set = TensorDataset(features[train_rows], target[train_rows])
    val_set = TensorDataset(features[val_rows], target[val_rows])
    train_loader = DataLoader(
        train_set,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        drop_last=len(train_set) > batch_size,
        generator=generator,
    )
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_set, batch_size=batch_size)

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = "cuda"
    elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        device = "mps"
    else:
        device = "cpu"
    print(f"Training on {device}: {len(train_set)} rows, {len(val_set)} for validation")
    if n_test:
        print(f"{n_test} rows are held out for the test")
    model.to(device)

    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)

    summary: dict[str, float] = {}
    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
        model.train()
        train_loss, seen = 0.0, 0
        for inputs, targets in train_loader:
            inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(inputs), targets)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            train_loss += loss.item() * len(inputs)
            seen += len(inputs)

        model.eval()
        val_loss, correct = 0.0, 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in val_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                outputs = model(inputs)
                val_loss += loss_fn(outputs, targets).item() * len(inputs)
                correct += (outputs.argmax(dim=1) == targets).sum().item()
        print(
            f"Epoch {epoch:3d}/{epochs}  train loss {train_loss / max(seen, 1):.4f}"
            f"  val loss {val_loss / len(val_set):.4f}  val acc {correct / len(val_set):.1%}"
        )
        summary = {
            "train_loss": train_loss / max(seen, 1),
            "val_loss": val_loss / len(val_set),
            "val_accuracy": correct / len(val_set),
        }
        if run is not None:
            run.log(epoch=epoch, **summary)

    if n_test:
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            inputs, targets = features[test_rows].to(device), target[test_rows].to(device)
            outputs = model(inputs)
            summary["test_loss"] = loss_fn(outputs, targets).item()
            summary["test_accuracy"] = (outputs.argmax(dim=1) == targets).float().mean().item()
        tested = [f"{key[5:]} {value:.4f}" for key, value in summary.items() if "test" in key]
        print("Test:", ", ".join(tested))
    if run is not None:
        run.finish(summary=summary)
    model.cpu()
    return mean, std


def save_model(
    model: nn.Module, path: str, header: list[str], mean: torch.Tensor, std: torch.Tensor
) -> None:
    """Save the weights together with what predict() needs to prepare new rows."""
    preprocessing = {
        "columns": header[:-1],  # the feature columns by name (empty: no header line)
        "target": header[-1] if header else "target",
        "mean": mean.tolist(),  # every feature is standardised: (value - mean) / std
        "std": std.tolist(),
        "task": "classification",
        "num_classes": NUM_CLASSES,
    }
    torch.save({"state_dict": model.state_dict(), "preprocessing": preprocessing}, path)
    print(f"Saved the weights and the preprocessing to {path}")


def predict(model: nn.Module, path: str, csv_path: str) -> None:
    """Print a prediction for every row of a CSV file, prepared like the training data.

    If both files have a header line, the feature columns are found by their names;
    otherwise they have to come first. Other columns (such as the target) are ignored.
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["state_dict"])
    model.eval()
    preprocessing = checkpoint["preprocessing"]
    columns = preprocessing["columns"]
    header, data = read_csv(csv_path)
    if columns and header:
        missing = [name for name in columns if name not in header]
        if missing:
            raise SystemExit(f"{csv_path} lacks the columns {', '.join(missing)}.")
        features = data[:, [header.index(name) for name in columns]]
    elif data.shape[1] >= NUM_FEATURES:
        features = data[:, :NUM_FEATURES]
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns, found {data.shape[1]}.")
    mean = torch.tensor(preprocessing["mean"])
    std = torch.tensor(preprocessing["std"])
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model((features - mean) / std)
    print(preprocessing["target"])
    for value in outputs.argmax(dim=1).tolist():
        print(value)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Logging to Brick DNN, only with the environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# The server and the saved network the runs belong to (BRICKDNN_URL and BRICKDNN_PROJECT
# override them). The token is never stored here: it is read from BRICKDNN_TOKEN.
BRICKDNN_URL = "https://brickdnn.com"
BRICKDNN_PROJECT = None


class BrickDNNRun:
    """A run logged to Brick DNN (see brickdnn/tracking.py), or an inert one without the
    environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN."""

    # Points are sent in batches: when this many are waiting, or after INTERVAL seconds.
    BATCH = 200
    INTERVAL = 2.0
    # Points kept while the server cannot be reached; failures in a row before giving up.
    BUFFER = 1000
    ATTEMPTS = 3
    RETRY_SECONDS = 10.0
    TIMEOUT = 5.0

    def __init__(self, url: str | None = None, token: str | None = None) -> None:
        url = os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_URL") or url or "https://brickdnn.com"
        self.url = url.strip().rstrip("/")
        self.token = (token if token is not None else os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_TOKEN", "")).strip()
        self.id: str | None = None
        self.active = bool(self.token)
        self.points: list[dict] = []
        self._create: dict = {}
        self._started = time.monotonic()
        self._sent = self._started  # the first batch waits INTERVAL too
        self._failures = 0
        self._retry_at = 0.0
        self._warned = False

    @classmethod
    def start(
        cls,
        name: str | None = None,
        config: dict | None = None,
        project: int | None = None,
        dataset: str | None = None,
        task: str | None = None,
        epochs: int | None = None,
        url: str | None = None,
        token: str | None = None,
    ) -> BrickDNNRun:
        """Create the run on the server (nothing happens without a token)."""
        run = cls(url, token)
        if not run.active:
            return run
        if os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_PROJECT", "").strip().isdigit():
            project = int(os.environ["BRICKDNN_PROJECT"].strip())
        body = {
            "name": os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_RUN_NAME") or name,
            "config": config or {},
            "project": project,
            "dataset": dataset,
            "task": task,
            "epochs": epochs,
            "client": "brickdnn-tracking/1",
        }
        run._create = {key: value for key, value in body.items() if value is not None}
        run._open()
        return run

    def _open(self) -> bool:
        """Create the run on the server if that has not worked yet."""
        if self.id is None and self.active and time.monotonic() >= self._retry_at:
            answer = self._send("POST", "/api/tracking/runs/", self._create)
            if isinstance(answer, dict) and isinstance(answer.get("id"), str):
                self.id = answer["id"]
                print(f"Brick DNN: logging this run to {self.url}/runs", file=sys.stderr)
        return self.id is not None

    def log(self, epoch: int | None = None, step: int | None = None, **metrics) -> None:
        """One point of the curves: ``epoch`` (or ``step``) and numbers such as
        ``train_loss``, ``val_loss`` or ``val_accuracy``; other values are left out."""
        if not self.active:
            return
        try:
            point: dict = {"time": round(time.monotonic() - self._started, 3)}
            if epoch is not None:
                point["epoch"] = int(epoch)
            if step is not None:
                point["step"] = int(step)
            for key, value in metrics.items():
                number = self._number(value)
                if number is not None:
                    point[str(key)] = number
            self.points.append(point)
            del self.points[: max(0, len(self.points) - self.BUFFER)]
            if len(self.points) >= self.BATCH or time.monotonic() - self._sent >= self.INTERVAL:
                self.flush()
        except Exception as error:  # logging never stops the training
            self._fail(error)

    def flush(self) -> None:
        """Send the points that wait."""
        if not self.active or not self.points or time.monotonic() < self._retry_at:
            return
        if not self._open():
            return
        while self.active and self.points:
            batch = self.points[: self.BATCH]
            if self._send("POST", f"/api/tracking/runs/{self.id}/log/", {"points": batch}) is None:
                return
            del self.points[: len(batch)]
            self._sent = time.monotonic()

    def finish(
        self, status: str = "completed", summary: dict | None = None, message: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """End the run: ``completed``, ``failed`` or ``stopped``, with its final numbers
        (e.g. ``{"test_accuracy": 0.93}``)."""
        if not self.active:
            return
        try:
            self._retry_at = 0.0
            self.flush()
            if self.active and self._open():
                numbers = {str(k): self._number(v) for k, v in (summary or {}).items()}
                body: dict = {
                    "status": status,
                    "summary": {k: v for k, v in numbers.items() if v is not None},
                }
                if message:
                    body["message"] = str(message)[:500]
                self._send("POST", f"/api/tracking/runs/{self.id}/finish/", body)
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        self.active = False

    def __enter__(self) -> BrickDNNRun:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, kind, error, traceback) -> bool:
        if kind is None:
            self.finish("completed")
        elif issubclass(kind, KeyboardInterrupt):
            self.finish("stopped", message="Stopped with Ctrl+C.")
        else:
            self.finish("failed", message=f"{kind.__name__}: {error}")
        return False  # an error goes on as before

    @staticmethod
    def _number(value) -> float | int | None:
        try:
            if hasattr(value, "item"):
                value = value.item()  # a tensor or a NumPy number
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
                return None
            return value if math.isfinite(value) else None
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _send(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict) -> dict | None:
        """The server's answer, or None if the request failed (warned once)."""
        try:
            request = urllib.request.Request(
                self.url + path,
                data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                method=method,
                headers={
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}",
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    "User-Agent": "brickdnn-tracking/1",
                },
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=self.TIMEOUT) as response:
                answer = json.loads(response.read().decode() or "{}")
            self._failures = 0
            return answer if isinstance(answer, dict) else {}
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            # Busy or broken for a moment: again later. Refused (token, limit, the run was
            # stopped in the app): for good.
            self._fail(error, final=error.code not in (408, 429) and error.code < 500)
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        return None

    def _fail(self, error: Exception, final: bool = False) -> None:
        self._failures += 1
        if not self._warned:
            self._warned = True
            detail = str(error)
            if isinstance(error, urllib.error.HTTPError):
                try:
                    detail = json.loads(error.read().decode()).get("detail") or detail
                except Exception:
                    detail = f"HTTP {error.code}"
            print(
                f"Brick DNN: could not log to {self.url} ({detail}). The training goes on"
                + ("." if final else "; logging is tried again a few times."),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        if final or self._failures >= self.ATTEMPTS:
            self.active = False
            self.points = []
        else:
            self._retry_at = time.monotonic() + self.RETRY_SECONDS


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="NeuralNetwork generated with Brick DNN")
    parser.add_argument("--csv", help="train on this CSV file (last column = target)")
    parser.add_argument("--predict", metavar="CSV", help="predict the rows of this file")
    parser.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-3, help="learning rate")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="for a repeatable run")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--test-split", type=float, default=0.0, help="share of the rows held out as a test set"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--save", default="model.pt", help="the trained model (--csv writes it, --predict reads it)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)  # the same initial weights for the same seed

    model = NeuralNetwork()
    if args.predict:
        predict(model, args.save, args.predict)
        return
    print(model)
    print(f"Trainable parameters: {count_parameters(model):,}")

    if args.csv:
        header, features, target = load_csv(args.csv)
        # Logged to Brick DNN only with the environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN.
        with BrickDNNRun.start(
            name="NeuralNetwork",
            config={
                "epochs": args.epochs,
                "batch_size": args.batch_size,
                "learning_rate": args.lr,
                "optimizer": "adam",
                "seed": args.seed,
                "loss": "cross_entropy",
                "val_split": 0.2,
                "test_split": args.test_split,
            },
            project=BRICKDNN_PROJECT,
            dataset=os.path.basename(args.csv),
            task="classification",
            epochs=args.epochs,
            url=BRICKDNN_URL,
        ) as run:
            mean, std = train(
                model,
                features,
                target,
                args.epochs,
                args.batch_size,
                args.lr,
                args.seed,
                args.test_split,
                run,
            )
        save_model(model, args.save, header, mean, std)
        return

    # Check the model with a random batch of 2 samples.
    model.eval()
    x = torch.randn(2, 784)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(x)
    print("Output shape:", tuple(out.shape))  # expected (2, 10)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""NeuralNetwork: generated with Brick DNN.

Input: (batch, 1, 28, 28)
Output: (batch, 10)
Trainable parameters: 421,642

Print the model and run it on a random batch:

    python this_file.py
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class NeuralNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.conv2d_1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 32, kernel_size=3, padding='same')
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.maxpool2d_1 = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2)
        self.conv2d_2 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding='same')
        self.relu_2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.maxpool2d_2 = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2)
        self.flatten_1 = nn.Flatten()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(3136, 128)
        self.relu_3 = nn.ReLU()
        self.dropout_1 = nn.Dropout(p=0.25)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(128, 10)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.conv2d_1(x)
        x = self.relu_1(x)
        x = self.maxpool2d_1(x)
        x = self.conv2d_2(x)
        x = self.relu_2(x)
        x = self.maxpool2d_2(x)
        x = self.flatten_1(x)
        x = self.linear_1(x)
        x = self.relu_3(x)
        x = self.dropout_1(x)
        x = self.linear_2(x)
        return x


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


def main() -> None:
    model = NeuralNetwork()
    print(model)
    print(f"Trainable parameters: {count_parameters(model):,}")

    # Check the model with a random batch of 2 samples.
    model.eval()
    x = torch.randn(2, 1, 28, 28)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(x)
    print("Output shape:", tuple(out.shape))  # expected (2, 10)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""NeuralNetwork: generated with Brick DNN.

Input: (batch, 3, 32, 32)
Output: (batch, 10)
Trainable parameters: 76,490

Print the model and run it on a random batch:

    python this_file.py
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class NeuralNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.conv2d_1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 64, kernel_size=3, padding='same', bias=False)
        self.batchnorm2d_1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.conv2d_2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 64, kernel_size=3, padding='same', bias=False)
        self.batchnorm2d_2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.relu_2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.conv2d_3 = nn.Conv2d(64, 64, kernel_size=3, padding='same', bias=False)
        self.batchnorm2d_3 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.relu_3 = nn.ReLU()
        self.avgpool_1 = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.flatten_1 = nn.Flatten()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(64, 10)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        conv2d_1 = self.conv2d_1(x)
        batchnorm2d_1 = self.batchnorm2d_1(conv2d_1)
        relu_1 = self.relu_1(batchnorm2d_1)
        conv2d_2 = self.conv2d_2(relu_1)
        batchnorm2d_2 = self.batchnorm2d_2(conv2d_2)
        relu_2 = self.relu_2(batchnorm2d_2)
        conv2d_3 = self.conv2d_3(relu_2)
        batchnorm2d_3 = self.batchnorm2d_3(conv2d_3)

# Built with Brick DNN: https://brickdnn.com, https://github.com/alexanderKuehling/brick-dnn
"""NeuralNetwork: generated with Brick DNN.

Input: (batch, 8)
Output: (batch, 1)
Trainable parameters: 2,817

Print the model and run it on a random batch:

    python this_file.py

Train it on a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature,
the last column is the target), then predict new rows with the saved model:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv --epochs 20
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv

--test-split 0.2 holds out a fifth of the rows and measures the model on them
once at the end.

Log the training to Brick DNN, to see its curves next to the runs trained there
(the runs page): create an API token on the page API tokens (one that may only
log runs is enough) and set it in the environment before you train:

    export BRICKDNN_TOKEN=<your token>
    python this_file.py --csv data.csv --epochs 20

It sends the loss and the metrics of every epoch, the settings, the name of the
CSV file and the test results to BRICKDNN_URL (default https://brickdnn.com). Without
BRICKDNN_TOKEN nothing is sent and the script runs offline with the same results;
a network error never stops the training. The token is never stored in this file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset


class NeuralNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(8, 64)
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.batchnorm1d_1 = nn.BatchNorm1d(64)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(64, 32)
        self.relu_2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.linear_3 = nn.Linear(32, 1)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.linear_1(x)
        x = self.relu_1(x)
        x = self.batchnorm1d_1(x)
        x = self.linear_2(x)
        x = self.relu_2(x)
        x = self.linear_3(x)
        return x


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Training on a CSV file, and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

NUM_FEATURES = 8
# regression: the model has a single output, the target column is a number


def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], torch.Tensor]:
    """Read a CSV file of numbers: the column names of its header line (an empty list if it
    has none) and the values."""
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = [row for row in csv.reader(f) if row]
    header: list[str] = []
    if rows:
        try:
            [float(value) for value in rows[0]]
        except ValueError:
            header, rows = [name.strip() for name in rows[0]], rows[1:]
    if not rows:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path} contains no data rows.")
    values = [[float(value) for value in row] for row in rows]
    return header, torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32)


def load_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Training data: every column but the last is a feature, the last one is the target."""
    header, data = read_csv(path)
    features, target = data[:, :-1], data[:, -1]
    if features.shape[1] != NUM_FEATURES:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns, found {features.shape[1]}.")
    return header, features, target.unsqueeze(1)


def train(
    model: nn.Module,
    features: torch.Tensor,
    target: torch.Tensor,
    epochs: int,
    batch_size: int,
    lr: float,
    seed: int,
    test_split: float = 0.0,
    run: BrickDNNRun | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Train on a random 80 % of the rows and validate on the rest (the split depends only
    on ``seed``). With ``test_split``, that share of the rows is held out as a test set and
    measured once at the end.

    Returns the mean and standard deviation that standardise the features. They come from
    the training rows only, and new data has to be standardised with them as well.
    """
    if len(features) < 4:
        raise SystemExit("The CSV file needs at least 4 rows (training + validation).")
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    order = torch.randperm(len(features), generator=generator)
    n_val = max(1, len(features) // 5)
    n_test = int(len(features) * test_split)
    if not 0 <= test_split < 1 or len(features) - n_val - n_test < 2:
        raise SystemExit("The test split leaves too few rows for training.")
    val_rows, test_rows = order[:n_val], order[n_val : n_val + n_test]
    train_rows = order[n_val + n_test :]

    mean = features[train_rows].mean(dim=0)
    std = features[train_rows].std(dim=0)
    std[std < 1e-8] = 1.0  # constant columns are left as they are
    features = (features - mean) / std

    train_set = TensorDataset(features[train_rows], target[train_rows])
    val_set = TensorDataset(features[val_rows], target[val_rows])
    train_loader = DataLoader(
        train_set,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        drop_last=len(train_set) > batch_size,
        generator=generator,
    )
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_set, batch_size=batch_size)

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = "cuda"
    elif torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        device = "mps"
    else:
        device = "cpu"
    print(f"Training on {device}: {len(train_set)} rows, {len(val_set)} for validation")
    if n_test:
        print(f"{n_test} rows are held out for the test")
    model.to(device)

    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)

    summary: dict[str, float] = {}
    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
        model.train()
        train_loss, seen = 0.0, 0
        for inputs, targets in train_loader:
            inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(model(inputs), targets)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            train_loss += loss.item() * len(inputs)
            seen += len(inputs)

        model.eval()
        val_loss, squared = 0.0, 0.0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for inputs, targets in val_loader:
                inputs, targets = inputs.to(device), targets.to(device)
                outputs = model(inputs)
                val_loss += loss_fn(outputs, targets).item() * len(inputs)
                squared += ((outputs - targets) ** 2).sum().item()
        print(
            f"Epoch {epoch:3d}/{epochs}  train loss {train_loss / max(seen, 1):.4f}"
            f"  val loss {val_loss / len(val_set):.4f}"
        )
        summary = {
            "train_loss": train_loss / max(seen, 1),
            "val_loss": val_loss / len(val_set),
            "val_rmse": (squared / len(val_set)) ** 0.5,
        }
        if run is not None:
            run.log(epoch=epoch, **summary)

    if n_test:
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            inputs, targets = features[test_rows].to(device), target[test_rows].to(device)
            outputs = model(inputs)
            summary["test_loss"] = loss_fn(outputs, targets).item()
            summary["test_rmse"] = ((outputs - targets) ** 2).mean().sqrt().item()
        tested = [f"{key[5:]} {value:.4f}" for key, value in summary.items() if "test" in key]
        print("Test:", ", ".join(tested))
    if run is not None:
        run.finish(summary=summary)
    model.cpu()
    return mean, std


def save_model(
    model: nn.Module, path: str, header: list[str], mean: torch.Tensor, std: torch.Tensor
) -> None:
    """Save the weights together with what predict() needs to prepare new rows."""
    preprocessing = {
        "columns": header[:-1],  # the feature columns by name (empty: no header line)
        "target": header[-1] if header else "target",
        "mean": mean.tolist(),  # every feature is standardised: (value - mean) / std
        "std": std.tolist(),
        "task": "regression",
    }
    torch.save({"state_dict": model.state_dict(), "preprocessing": preprocessing}, path)
    print(f"Saved the weights and the preprocessing to {path}")


def predict(model: nn.Module, path: str, csv_path: str) -> None:
    """Print a prediction for every row of a CSV file, prepared like the training data.

    If both files have a header line, the feature columns are found by their names;
    otherwise they have to come first. Other columns (such as the target) are ignored.
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint["state_dict"])
    model.eval()
    preprocessing = checkpoint["preprocessing"]
    columns = preprocessing["columns"]
    header, data = read_csv(csv_path)
    if columns and header:
        missing = [name for name in columns if name not in header]
        if missing:
            raise SystemExit(f"{csv_path} lacks the columns {', '.join(missing)}.")
        features = data[:, [header.index(name) for name in columns]]
    elif data.shape[1] >= NUM_FEATURES:
        features = data[:, :NUM_FEATURES]
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns, found {data.shape[1]}.")
    mean = torch.tensor(preprocessing["mean"])
    std = torch.tensor(preprocessing["std"])
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model((features - mean) / std)
    print(preprocessing["target"])
    for value in outputs[:, 0].tolist():
        print(value)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Logging to Brick DNN, only with the environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# The server and the saved network the runs belong to (BRICKDNN_URL and BRICKDNN_PROJECT
# override them). The token is never stored here: it is read from BRICKDNN_TOKEN.
BRICKDNN_URL = "https://brickdnn.com"
BRICKDNN_PROJECT = None


class BrickDNNRun:
    """A run logged to Brick DNN (see brickdnn/tracking.py), or an inert one without the
    environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN."""

    # Points are sent in batches: when this many are waiting, or after INTERVAL seconds.
    BATCH = 200
    INTERVAL = 2.0
    # Points kept while the server cannot be reached; failures in a row before giving up.
    BUFFER = 1000
    ATTEMPTS = 3
    RETRY_SECONDS = 10.0
    TIMEOUT = 5.0

    def __init__(self, url: str | None = None, token: str | None = None) -> None:
        url = os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_URL") or url or "https://brickdnn.com"
        self.url = url.strip().rstrip("/")
        self.token = (token if token is not None else os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_TOKEN", "")).strip()
        self.id: str | None = None
        self.active = bool(self.token)
        self.points: list[dict] = []
        self._create: dict = {}
        self._started = time.monotonic()
        self._sent = self._started  # the first batch waits INTERVAL too
        self._failures = 0
        self._retry_at = 0.0
        self._warned = False

    @classmethod
    def start(
        cls,
        name: str | None = None,
        config: dict | None = None,
        project: int | None = None,
        dataset: str | None = None,
        task: str | None = None,
        epochs: int | None = None,
        url: str | None = None,
        token: str | None = None,
    ) -> BrickDNNRun:
        """Create the run on the server (nothing happens without a token)."""
        run = cls(url, token)
        if not run.active:
            return run
        if os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_PROJECT", "").strip().isdigit():
            project = int(os.environ["BRICKDNN_PROJECT"].strip())
        body = {
            "name": os.environ.get("BRICKDNN_RUN_NAME") or name,
            "config": config or {},
            "project": project,
            "dataset": dataset,
            "task": task,
            "epochs": epochs,
            "client": "brickdnn-tracking/1",
        }
        run._create = {key: value for key, value in body.items() if value is not None}
        run._open()
        return run

    def _open(self) -> bool:
        """Create the run on the server if that has not worked yet."""
        if self.id is None and self.active and time.monotonic() >= self._retry_at:
            answer = self._send("POST", "/api/tracking/runs/", self._create)
            if isinstance(answer, dict) and isinstance(answer.get("id"), str):
                self.id = answer["id"]
                print(f"Brick DNN: logging this run to {self.url}/runs", file=sys.stderr)
        return self.id is not None

    def log(self, epoch: int | None = None, step: int | None = None, **metrics) -> None:
        """One point of the curves: ``epoch`` (or ``step``) and numbers such as
        ``train_loss``, ``val_loss`` or ``val_accuracy``; other values are left out."""
        if not self.active:
            return
        try:
            point: dict = {"time": round(time.monotonic() - self._started, 3)}
            if epoch is not None:
                point["epoch"] = int(epoch)
            if step is not None:
                point["step"] = int(step)
            for key, value in metrics.items():
                number = self._number(value)
                if number is not None:
                    point[str(key)] = number
            self.points.append(point)
            del self.points[: max(0, len(self.points) - self.BUFFER)]
            if len(self.points) >= self.BATCH or time.monotonic() - self._sent >= self.INTERVAL:
                self.flush()
        except Exception as error:  # logging never stops the training
            self._fail(error)

    def flush(self) -> None:
        """Send the points that wait."""
        if not self.active or not self.points or time.monotonic() < self._retry_at:
            return
        if not self._open():
            return
        while self.active and self.points:
            batch = self.points[: self.BATCH]
            if self._send("POST", f"/api/tracking/runs/{self.id}/log/", {"points": batch}) is None:
                return
            del self.points[: len(batch)]
            self._sent = time.monotonic()

    def finish(
        self, status: str = "completed", summary: dict | None = None, message: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """End the run: ``completed``, ``failed`` or ``stopped``, with its final numbers
        (e.g. ``{"test_accuracy": 0.93}``)."""
        if not self.active:
            return
        try:
            self._retry_at = 0.0
            self.flush()
            if self.active and self._open():
                numbers = {str(k): self._number(v) for k, v in (summary or {}).items()}
                body: dict = {
                    "status": status,
                    "summary": {k: v for k, v in numbers.items() if v is not None},
                }
                if message:
                    body["message"] = str(message)[:500]
                self._send("POST", f"/api/tracking/runs/{self.id}/finish/", body)
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        self.active = False

    def __enter__(self) -> BrickDNNRun:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, kind, error, traceback) -> bool:
        if kind is None:
            self.finish("completed")
        elif issubclass(kind, KeyboardInterrupt):
            self.finish("stopped", message="Stopped with Ctrl+C.")
        else:
            self.finish("failed", message=f"{kind.__name__}: {error}")
        return False  # an error goes on as before

    @staticmethod
    def _number(value) -> float | int | None:
        try:
            if hasattr(value, "item"):
                value = value.item()  # a tensor or a NumPy number
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
                return None
            return value if math.isfinite(value) else None
        except Exception:
            return None

    def _send(self, method: str, path: str, body: dict) -> dict | None:
        """The server's answer, or None if the request failed (warned once)."""
        try:
            request = urllib.request.Request(
                self.url + path,
                data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                method=method,
                headers={
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}",
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    "User-Agent": "brickdnn-tracking/1",
                },
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=self.TIMEOUT) as response:
                answer = json.loads(response.read().decode() or "{}")
            self._failures = 0
            return answer if isinstance(answer, dict) else {}
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            # Busy or broken for a moment: again later. Refused (token, limit, the run was
            # stopped in the app): for good.
            self._fail(error, final=error.code not in (408, 429) and error.code < 500)
        except Exception as error:
            self._fail(error)
        return None

    def _fail(self, error: Exception, final: bool = False) -> None:
        self._failures += 1
        if not self._warned:
            self._warned = True
            detail = str(error)
            if isinstance(error, urllib.error.HTTPError):
                try:
                    detail = json.loads(error.read().decode()).get("detail") or detail
                except Exception:
                    detail = f"HTTP {error.code}"
            print(
                f"Brick DNN: could not log to {self.url} ({detail}). The training goes on"
                + ("." if final else "; logging is tried again a few times."),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        if final or self._failures >= self.ATTEMPTS:
            self.active = False
            self.points = []
        else:
            self._retry_at = time.monotonic() + self.RETRY_SECONDS


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="NeuralNetwork generated with Brick DNN")
    parser.add_argument("--csv", help="train on this CSV file (last column = target)")
    parser.add_argument("--predict", metavar="CSV", help="predict the rows of this file")
    parser.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-3, help="learning rate")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="for a repeatable run")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--test-split", type=float, default=0.0, help="share of the rows held out as a test set"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--save", default="model.pt", help="the trained model (--csv writes it, --predict reads it)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)  # the same initial weights for the same seed

    model = NeuralNetwork()
    if args.predict:
        predict(model, args.save, args.predict)
        return
    print(model)
    print(f"Trainable parameters: {count_parameters(model):,}")

    if args.csv:
        header, features, target = load_csv(args.csv)
        # Logged to Brick DNN only with the environment variable BRICKDNN_TOKEN.
        with BrickDNNRun.start(
            name="NeuralNetwork",
            config={
                "epochs": args.epochs,
                "batch_size": args.batch_size,
                "learning_rate": args.lr,
                "optimizer": "adam",
                "seed": args.seed,
                "loss": "mse",
                "val_split": 0.2,
                "test_split": args.test_split,
            },
            project=BRICKDNN_PROJECT,
            dataset=os.path.basename(args.csv),
            task="regression",
            epochs=args.epochs,
            url=BRICKDNN_URL,
        ) as run:
            mean, std = train(
                model,
                features,
                target,
                args.epochs,
                args.batch_size,
                args.lr,
                args.seed,
                args.test_split,
                run,
            )
        save_model(model, args.save, header, mean, std)
        return

    # Check the model with a random batch of 2 samples.
    model.eval()
    x = torch.randn(2, 8)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(x)
    print("Output shape:", tuple(out.shape))  # expected (2, 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""NeuralNetwork: generated with Brick DNN.

Input x_1: (batch, 1, 28, 28)
Input x_2: (batch, 10)
Output: (batch, 1)
Trainable parameters: 50,497

Print the model and run it on a random batch:

    python this_file.py
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class NeuralNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.flatten_1 = nn.Flatten()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(784, 64)
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(10, 16)
        self.relu_2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.linear_3 = nn.Linear(80, 1)

    def forward(self, x_1: torch.Tensor, x_2: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        flatten_1 = self.flatten_1(x_1)
        linear_1 = self.linear_1(flatten_1)
        relu_1 = self.relu_1(linear_1)
        linear_2 = self.linear_2(x_2)
        relu_2 = self.relu_2(linear_2)
        concat_1 = torch.cat([relu_1, relu_2], dim=-1)
        linear_3 = self.linear_3(concat_1)
        return linear_3


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)


def main() -> None:
    model = NeuralNetwork()
    print(model)
    print(f"Trainable parameters: {count_parameters(model):,}")

    # Check the model with a random batch of 2 samples.
    model.eval()
    x_1 = torch.randn(2, 1, 28, 28)
    x_2 = torch.randn(2, 10)
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(x_1, x_2)

# Built with Brick DNN: https://brickdnn.com, https://github.com/alexanderKuehling/brick-dnn
"""Gaussian process regression: generated with Brick DNN.

A scikit-learn model for 8 numeric features: they are standardised, then
GaussianProcessRegressor predicts one number per row.

Kernel (the starting point; fitting optimises its hyperparameters):
    ConstantKernel(constant_value=1.0) * RBF(length_scale=1.0)
    + WhiteKernel(noise_level=0.1)

Print the model and fit it to random data:

    python this_file.py

Fit it to a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature, the last column is
the target), then predict new rows with the saved model:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv
"""

import argparse
import csv
import time

import joblib
import numpy as np
from sklearn.gaussian_process import GaussianProcessRegressor
from sklearn.gaussian_process.kernels import RBF, ConstantKernel, WhiteKernel
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

NUM_FEATURES = 8


def make_model() -> Pipeline:
    """Standardise the features (with the mean and standard deviation of the data
    it is fitted to), then fit GaussianProcessRegressor."""
    constant = ConstantKernel(constant_value=1.0)
    rbf = RBF(length_scale=1.0)
    white = WhiteKernel(noise_level=0.1)
    kernel = constant * rbf + white
    model = GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=kernel, alpha=1e-10, normalize_y=True)
    return Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()), ("model", model)])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# CSV files: fitting, saving and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    """Read a CSV file: the column names of its header line (an empty list if it has none)
    and the rows (as text)."""
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = [row for row in csv.reader(f) if row]
    header: list[str] = []
    if rows:
        cells = rows[0][:-1] or rows[0]  # the last column (the target) may hold text
        try:
            [float(value) for value in cells]
        except ValueError:
            header, rows = [name.strip() for name in rows[0]], rows[1:]
    if not rows:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path} contains no data rows.")
    return header, rows


def numbers(rows: list[list[str]], path: str) -> np.ndarray:
    try:
        return np.array([[float(value) for value in row] for row in rows])
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: {exc}") from None


def load_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Training data: every column but the last is a feature, the last one is the target."""
    header, rows = read_csv(path)
    if any(len(row) != NUM_FEATURES + 1 for row in rows):
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns and the target in every row.")
    features = numbers([row[:-1] for row in rows], path)
    target = numbers([row[-1:] for row in rows], path)[:, 0]
    return header, features, target


def fit(model: Pipeline, features: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, seed: int) -> None:
    """Fit on a random 80 % of the rows and validate on the rest (the split depends only on
    ``seed``). The StandardScaler of the pipeline learns from the training rows only."""
    if len(features) < 4:
        raise SystemExit("The CSV file needs at least 4 rows (training + validation).")
    order = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(len(features))
    n_val = max(1, len(features) // 5)
    val_rows, train_rows = order[:n_val], order[n_val:]
    print(f"Fitting on {len(train_rows)} rows, {len(val_rows)} for validation")
    started = time.perf_counter()
    model.fit(features[train_rows], target[train_rows])
    print(f"Fitted in {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f} s")
    errors = model.predict(features[val_rows]) - target[val_rows]
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(errors**2)))
    spread = float(np.sum((target[val_rows] - target[val_rows].mean()) ** 2))
    r2 = 1 - float(np.sum(errors**2)) / spread if spread > 0 else float("nan")
    print(f"Validation RMSE {rmse:.4g}, R² {r2:.3f}")
    gp = model.named_steps["model"]
    print(f"Learned kernel: {gp.kernel_}")
    print(f"Log marginal likelihood: {gp.log_marginal_likelihood_value_:.4g}")


def save_model(model: Pipeline, path: str, header: list[str]) -> None:
    """Save the fitted pipeline with what predict() needs to read new rows. joblib files
    are pickles: only load files you trust."""
    bundle = {
        "format": "brickdnn-sklearn-1",
        "model": model,
        "columns": header[:-1],  # the feature columns by name (empty: no header line)
        "target": header[-1] if header else "target",
        "task": "regression",
        "class_names": None,
    }
    joblib.dump(bundle, path)
    print(f"Saved the fitted model to {path}")


def predict(path: str, csv_path: str) -> None:
    """Print a prediction for every row of a CSV file.

    If both the saved model and the file have a header line, the feature columns are found
    by their names; otherwise they have to come first. Other columns (such as the target)
    are ignored. The pipeline standardises the features like the training data.
    """
    bundle = joblib.load(path)  # a pickle: only load files you trust
    model, columns = bundle["model"], bundle["columns"]
    header, rows = read_csv(csv_path)
    if columns and header:
        missing = [name for name in columns if name not in header]
        if missing:
            raise SystemExit(f"{csv_path} lacks the columns {', '.join(missing)}.")
        rows = [[row[header.index(name)] for name in columns] for row in rows]
    elif all(len(row) >= NUM_FEATURES for row in rows):
        rows = [row[:NUM_FEATURES] for row in rows]
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns.")
    features = numbers(rows, csv_path)
    # The Gaussian process also says how uncertain it is: one standard deviation.
    mean, std = model.predict(features, return_std=True)
    print(f"{bundle['target']},std")
    for value, spread in zip(mean, std):
        print(f"{value:.6g},{spread:.6g}")


def demo(model: Pipeline) -> None:
    """Fit the model to 40 random rows and predict two of them (shows that it works)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    features = rng.normal(size=(40, NUM_FEATURES))
    target = features[:, 0] + np.sin(2 * features[:, -1])
    model.fit(features, target)
    print("Predictions for 2 random rows:", model.predict(features[:2]))


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Gaussian process regression, generated with Brick DNN"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--csv", help="fit the model to this CSV file (last column = target)")
    parser.add_argument("--predict", metavar="CSV", help="predict the rows of this file")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="for a repeatable split")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--save",
        default="model.joblib",
        help="the fitted model (--csv writes it, --predict reads it)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.predict:
        predict(args.save, args.predict)
        return
    model = make_model()
    print(model)
    if args.csv:
        header, features, target = load_csv(args.csv)
        fit(model, features, target, args.seed)
        save_model(model, args.save, header)
        return
    demo(model)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Built with Brick DNN: https://brickdnn.com, https://github.com/alexanderKuehling/brick-dnn
"""Support vector classification: generated with Brick DNN.

A scikit-learn model for 4 numeric features: they are standardised, then SVC predicts the
class of each row. Platt scaling (5-fold cross-validation) turns the SVM's scores into class
probabilities.

Print the model and fit it to random data:

    python this_file.py

Fit it to a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature, the last column is
the target), then predict new rows with the saved model:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv
"""

import argparse
import csv
import time

import joblib
import numpy as np
from sklearn.calibration import CalibratedClassifierCV
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVC

NUM_FEATURES = 4


def make_model() -> Pipeline:
    """Standardise the features (with the mean and standard deviation of the data
    it is fitted to), then fit SVC."""
    svc = SVC(kernel="rbf", C=1.0, gamma="scale")
    # Platt scaling: 5-fold cross-validation turns the scores into probabilities.
    model = CalibratedClassifierCV(svc, ensemble=False)
    return Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()), ("model", model)])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# CSV files: fitting, saving and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    """Read a CSV file: the column names of its header line (an empty list if it has none)
    and the rows (as text)."""
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = [row for row in csv.reader(f) if row]
    header: list[str] = []
    if rows:
        cells = rows[0][:-1] or rows[0]  # the last column (the target) may hold text
        try:

"""Stacking regression: generated with Brick DNN.

A scikit-learn ensemble for 8 numeric features: they are standardised, then
StackingRegressor combines 3 models (boosting: HistGradientBoostingRegressor, svr: SVR, gp:
GaussianProcessRegressor) and predicts one number per row. RidgeCV learns from their
predictions for rows they were not fitted on (5-fold cross-validation) how to combine them.

Kernel of gp (the starting point; fitting optimises it):
    RBF(length_scale=1.0)
    + WhiteKernel(noise_level=0.1)

Print the model and fit it to random data:

    python this_file.py

Fit it to a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature, the last column is
the target), then predict new rows with the saved model:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv
"""

import argparse
import csv
import time

import joblib
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor, StackingRegressor
from sklearn.gaussian_process import GaussianProcessRegressor
from sklearn.gaussian_process.kernels import RBF, WhiteKernel
from sklearn.linear_model import RidgeCV
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVR

NUM_FEATURES = 8


def make_model() -> Pipeline:
    """Standardise the features (with the mean and standard deviation of the data
    it is fitted to), then fit StackingRegressor with its 3 models."""
    boosting = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(
        learning_rate=0.1,
        max_iter=200,
        max_leaf_nodes=31,
        max_depth=None,
        min_samples_leaf=20,
        l2_regularization=0.0,
        early_stopping="auto",
        random_state=0,
    )
    svr = SVR(kernel="rbf", C=1.0, gamma="scale", epsilon=0.1)
    gp_kernel = RBF(length_scale=1.0) + WhiteKernel(noise_level=0.1)
    gp = GaussianProcessRegressor(kernel=gp_kernel, alpha=1e-10, normalize_y=True)
    model = StackingRegressor(
        estimators=[("boosting", boosting), ("svr", svr), ("gp", gp)],
        final_estimator=RidgeCV(),
        cv=5,
        passthrough=False,
    )
    return Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()), ("model", model)])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# CSV files: fitting, saving and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

    if rows:

        try:

    if not rows:

def fit(model: Pipeline, features: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, seed: int) -> None:

examples.code:
# Built with Brick DNN: https://brickdnn.com, https://github.com/alexanderKuehling/brick-dnn
"""Gradient boosting classification on learned features: generated with Brick DNN.

Neural layers (FeatureExtractor) turn 8 numeric features into 32 learned features;
HistGradientBoostingClassifier is fitted on them and predicts the class of each row. The
training has two phases: first the neural layers learn with a temporary linear head on the
target (with --frozen they keep their random initial weights), then the head is dropped and
the classical model is fitted on the features of the training rows.

Print the models and fit them to random data:

    python this_file.py

Train on a CSV file (every column but the last is a feature, the last column is
the target); this writes features.pt (the neural layers) and model.joblib (the
classical model). Then predict new rows with both:

    python this_file.py --csv data.csv --epochs 20
    python this_file.py --predict new_data.csv
"""

import argparse
import csv
import time

import joblib
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

NUM_FEATURES = 8  # input columns of the CSV file
NUM_LEARNED = 32  # features the neural layers learn


class FeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(8, 64)
        self.relu_1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.learned_features = nn.Linear(64, 32)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.linear_1(x)
        x = self.relu_1(x)
        x = self.learned_features(x)
        return x


def make_model() -> Pipeline:
    """Standardise the features (with the mean and standard deviation of the data
    it is fitted to), then fit HistGradientBoostingClassifier."""
    model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
        learning_rate=0.1,
        max_iter=200,
        max_leaf_nodes=31,
        max_depth=None,
        min_samples_leaf=20,
        l2_regularization=0.0,
        early_stopping="auto",
        random_state=0,
    )
    return Pipeline([("scale", StandardScaler()), ("model", model)])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The two phases: learning the features, then fitting the classical model
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def extract(extractor: nn.Module, inputs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The learned features of every row (or sample): the output of the neural layers,
    computed in batches without gradients."""
    extractor.eval()
    x = torch.as_tensor(inputs, dtype=torch.float32)
    with torch.no_grad():
        parts = [extractor(x[i : i + 1024]) for i in range(0, len(x), 1024)]
    if not parts:
        return np.empty((0, NUM_LEARNED))
    return torch.cat(parts).double().numpy()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# CSV files: fitting, saving and predictions for new rows
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def read_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    """Read a CSV file: the column names of its header line (an empty list if it has none)
    and the rows (as text)."""
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = [row for row in csv.reader(f) if row]
    header: list[str] = []
    if rows:
        cells = rows[0][:-1] or rows[0]  # the last column (the target) may hold text
        try:
            [float(value) for value in cells]
        except ValueError:
            header, rows = [name.strip() for name in rows[0]], rows[1:]
    if not rows:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path} contains no data rows.")
    return header, rows


def numbers(rows: list[list[str]], path: str) -> np.ndarray:
    try:
        return np.array([[float(value) for value in row] for row in rows])
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(f"{path}: {exc}") from None


def load_csv(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Training data: every column but the last is a feature, the last one is the target."""
    header, rows = read_csv(path)
    if any(len(row) != NUM_FEATURES + 1 for row in rows):
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} feature columns and the target in every row.")
    features = numbers([row[:-1] for row in rows], path)
    target = np.array([row[-1].strip() for row in rows])  # the class labels
    return header, features, target


def split_rows(n: int, seed: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """A random 80 % of the rows for training, the rest for validation (fixed by ``seed``).
    Both phases use the same split."""
    if n < 4:
        raise SystemExit("The CSV file needs at least 4 rows (training + validation).")
    order = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(n)
    n_val = max(1, n // 5)
    return order[n_val:], order[:n_val]


def standardise(features: np.ndarray, train_rows: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """The mean and standard deviation of the training rows. New rows are standardised with
    them as well, before the neural layers."""
    mean = features[train_rows].mean(axis=0)
    std = features[train_rows].std(axis=0)
    std[std < 1e-8] = 1.0  # constant columns are left as they are
    return mean, std


def learn_features(
    extractor: FeatureExtractor,
    features: np.ndarray,
    target: np.ndarray,
    train_rows: np.ndarray,
    val_rows: np.ndarray,
    epochs: int,
    batch_size: int,
    lr: float,
    seed: int,
) -> None:
    """Phase 1: train the neural layers with a temporary linear head on the target, then
    drop the head. ``features`` are standardised."""
    # Classification: one output per class and the cross-entropy loss.
    classes, labels = np.unique(target, return_inverse=True)
    y = torch.as_tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
    head = nn.Linear(NUM_LEARNED, len(classes))
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    x = torch.as_tensor(features, dtype=torch.float32)
    train, val = torch.as_tensor(train_rows), torch.as_tensor(val_rows)
    network = nn.Sequential(extractor, head)
    loader = DataLoader(
        TensorDataset(x[train], y[train]),
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=True,
        drop_last=len(train) > batch_size,
        generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed),
    )
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(network.parameters(), lr=lr)
    print(f"Learning the features on {len(train)} rows, {len(val)} for validation")
    for epoch in range(1, epochs + 1):
        network.train()
        total, seen = 0.0, 0
        for inputs, targets in loader:
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = loss_fn(network(inputs), targets)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            total += loss.item() * len(inputs)
            seen += len(inputs)
        network.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            val_loss = loss_fn(network(x[val]), y[val]).item()
        print(
            f"Epoch {epoch:3d}/{epochs}  train loss {total / max(seen, 1):.4f}"
            f"  val loss {val_loss:.4f}"
        )


def fit(
    model: Pipeline,
    features: np.ndarray,
    target: np.ndarray,
    train_rows: np.ndarray,
    val_rows: np.ndarray,
) -> None:
    """Phase 2: fit the classical model on the learned features of the training rows and
    validate it on the other rows. Its StandardScaler learns from the training rows only."""
    print(f"Fitting on the {features.shape[1]} learned features of {len(train_rows)} rows")
    started = time.perf_counter()
    model.fit(features[train_rows], target[train_rows])
    print(f"Fitted in {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f} s")
    accuracy = float(np.mean(model.predict(features[val_rows]) == target[val_rows]))
    print(f"Validation accuracy {accuracy:.1%}")
    boosting = model.named_steps["model"]
    # Early stopping may end before max_iter.
    print(f"Boosting iterations: {boosting.n_iter_} of at most {boosting.max_iter}")


def save_model(
    extractor: FeatureExtractor,
    model: Pipeline,
    weights_path: str,
    model_path: str,
    header: list[str],
    mean: np.ndarray,
    std: np.ndarray,
) -> None:
    """Save the neural layers with the preprocessing of the input columns (PyTorch) and the
    fitted classical model (joblib, a pickle: only load files you trust)."""
    preprocessing = {
        "columns": header[:-1],  # the input columns by name (empty: no header line)
        "target": header[-1] if header else "target",
        "mean": mean.tolist(),  # every input column is standardised: (value - mean) / std
        "std": std.tolist(),
    }
    torch.save({"state_dict": extractor.state_dict(), "preprocessing": preprocessing}, weights_path)
    bundle = {
        "format": "brickdnn-sklearn-1",
        "model": model,
        "columns": [f"feature_{i + 1}" for i in range(NUM_LEARNED)],  # the learned features
        "target": preprocessing["target"],
        "task": "classification",
        # one name per column of model.predict_proba()
        "class_names": [str(name) for name in model.classes_],
        "hybrid": {"features": NUM_LEARNED, "input_columns": preprocessing["columns"]},
    }
    joblib.dump(bundle, model_path)
    print(f"Saved the neural layers to {weights_path} and the classical model to {model_path}")


def predict(weights_path: str, model_path: str, csv_path: str) -> None:
    """Print a prediction for every row of a CSV file: standardise the input columns like
    the training rows, compute the learned features, then let the classical model predict.

    If both the saved preprocessing and the file have a header line, the input columns are
    found by their names; otherwise they have to come first. Other columns are ignored.
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(weights_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    extractor = FeatureExtractor()
    extractor.load_state_dict(checkpoint["state_dict"])
    preprocessing = checkpoint["preprocessing"]
    bundle = joblib.load(model_path)  # a pickle: only load files you trust
    model, columns = bundle["model"], preprocessing["columns"]
    header, rows = read_csv(csv_path)
    if columns and header:
        missing = [name for name in columns if name not in header]
        if missing:
            raise SystemExit(f"{csv_path} lacks the columns {', '.join(missing)}.")
        rows = [[row[header.index(name)] for name in columns] for row in rows]
    elif all(len(row) >= NUM_FEATURES for row in rows):
        rows = [row[:NUM_FEATURES] for row in rows]
    else:
        raise SystemExit(f"Expected {NUM_FEATURES} input columns.")
    inputs = numbers(rows, csv_path)
    mean, std = np.asarray(preprocessing["mean"]), np.asarray(preprocessing["std"])
    features = extract(extractor, (inputs - mean) / std)
    probabilities = model.predict_proba(features)
    names = bundle["class_names"]
    print(f"{bundle['target']},probability")
    for row in probabilities:
        best = int(np.argmax(row))
        print(f"{names[best]},{row[best]:.4f}")


def demo(extractor: FeatureExtractor, model: Pipeline) -> None:
    """Compute the features of 40 random samples with the untrained neural layers, fit the
    model on them and predict two (shows that both parts work together)."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    learned = extract(extractor, rng.normal(size=(40, NUM_FEATURES)))
    target = np.where(learned[:, 0] + learned[:, -1] > 0, "yes", "no")
    model.fit(learned, target)
    print("Predictions for 2 random samples:", model.predict(learned[:2]))


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Gradient boosting classification on learned features, generated with Brick DNN"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--csv", help="train on this CSV file (last column = target)")
    parser.add_argument("--predict", metavar="CSV", help="predict the rows of this file")
    parser.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=1e-3, help="learning rate")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--frozen",
        action="store_true",
        help="keep the random initial weights of the neural layers (no training)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="for a repeatable run")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--weights", default="features.pt", help="the neural layers (--csv writes it)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--save", default="model.joblib", help="the classical model (--csv writes it)"
    )
